# Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to run a single clone-censor-weight (CCW)
target trial emulation using the `CloneCensorWeight` package. We use the OHDSI
[Capr](https://ohdsi.github.io/Capr/) package to define cohorts in R and
[CohortGenerator](https://ohdsi.github.io/CohortGenerator/) to instantiate
them on a database before running the analysis.

## Clinical question

**Among adults with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis (PsA), or
ulcerative colitis (UC) who newly initiate a JAK inhibitor, does receiving the
recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) within 90 days of JAK inhibitor
initiation reduce incident herpes zoster over two years, compared with no
vaccination during that window?**

## Why CCW is needed

JAK inhibitors substantially increase herpes zoster risk. A naive comparison
of vaccinated vs. unvaccinated JAK inhibitor users is biased for two reasons.

**Immortal time bias.** A patient vaccinated on day 60 has survived 60 days
without herpes zoster before entering the "vaccinated" group; a naive analysis
credits the vaccine with those event-free days.

**Informative censoring.** Within the CCW framework, a clone assigned to the
"vaccinate within 90 days" arm is artificially censored when the patient has
not yet vaccinated. Because healthier, more care-engaged patients are more
likely to vaccinate promptly, the subjects who *survive* in the vaccinated arm
are a positively selected subset. Inverse probability of censoring weighting
(IPCW) corrects for this selection.

CCW addresses both problems. Every patient is cloned into both arms at cohort
entry, so baseline balance is guaranteed. Each clone is censored only when its
observed behavior deviates from its assigned protocol. IPCW restores the
target population.

## Target trial specification

| Element | Specification |
|---|---|
| Eligibility | Adults with RA, PsA, or UC; new JAK inhibitor user (no use in prior 365 days); no prior RZV in past 5 years; ≥ 365 days prior observation |
| Treatment arm | Receive first dose of RZV within 90 days of JAK inhibitor start |
| Comparator arm | No RZV within the first 90 days |
| Assignment | Cloning at JAK inhibitor start date |
| Follow-up | Until herpes zoster, death, disenrollment, or 730 days |
| Primary outcome | Incident herpes zoster |
| Causal contrast | Per-protocol effect of early vaccination vs. deferred/no vaccination |

---

# Connecting to the database

`CloneCensorWeight` uses `DatabaseConnector` to communicate with the CDM.
Adjust the connection details for your platform.

```{r connect}
library(CloneCensorWeight)
library(Capr)
library(CohortGenerator)

connectionDetails <- DatabaseConnector::createConnectionDetails(
  dbms    = "postgresql",
  server  = "localhost/ohdsi",
  user    = "joe",
  password = "supersecret"
)

cdmDatabaseSchema    <- "cdm_v54"
cohortDatabaseSchema <- "scratch"
cohortTable          <- "ccw_jak_rzv"

options(sqlRenderTempEmulationSchema = NULL)
```

---

# Defining cohorts with Capr

We define four cohort types:

1. **Index cohort** — new JAK inhibitor users with an autoimmune indication
2. **Exposure cohort** — first dose of RZV (used for both arms)
3. **Primary outcome cohort** — incident herpes zoster
4. **Negative control outcome cohorts** — for empirical calibration

Concept IDs can be browsed and verified at
[Athena](https://athena.ohdsi.org/).

## Concept sets

```{r concept-sets}
# JAK inhibitors (tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib, filgotinib,
# abrocitinib — include all descendants to capture branded formulations)
jakInhibitors <- cs(
  descendants(42873017L,  # tofacitinib
              1510448L,   # baricitinib
              2213473L,   # upadacitinib
              2109604L,   # filgotinib
              2215702L),  # abrocitinib
  name = "JAK inhibitors"
)

# Autoimmune indications
rheumatoidArthritis <- cs(descendants(80809L),  name = "Rheumatoid arthritis")
psoriaticArthritis  <- cs(descendants(73553L),  name = "Psoriatic arthritis")
ulcerativeColitis   <- cs(descendants(81893L),  name = "Ulcerative colitis")

# Recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix only — excludes live zoster vaccine)
rzv <- cs(
  descendants(1160056L,   # recombinant zoster vaccine antigen
              1160057L),  # zoster vaccine recombinant
  name = "Recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix)"
)

# Herpes zoster
herpesZoster <- cs(descendants(4067760L), name = "Herpes zoster")
```

## Index cohort: new JAK inhibitor users

Eligible patients must have an autoimmune indication (RA, PsA, or UC) on or
before their JAK inhibitor start date, at least 365 days of prior observation,
no JAK inhibitor use in the prior 365 days, and no prior RZV in the past
5 years.

```{r index-cohort}
jakNewUsers <- cohort(
  entry = entry(
    drugExposure(jakInhibitors, firstOccurrence()),
    observationWindow = continuousObservation(priorDays = 365L)
  ),
  attrition = attrition(
    "Autoimmune indication" = withAny(
      atLeast(1, conditionOccurrence(rheumatoidArthritis),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-Inf, 0))),
      atLeast(1, conditionOccurrence(psoriaticArthritis),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-Inf, 0))),
      atLeast(1, conditionOccurrence(ulcerativeColitis),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-Inf, 0)))
    ),
    "No prior JAK inhibitor" = withAll(
      exactly(0, drugExposure(jakInhibitors),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-365L, -1L)))
    ),
    "No prior RZV" = withAll(
      exactly(0, drugExposure(rzv),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-1825L, -1L)))  # 5 years
    )
  ),
  exit = exit(endStrategy = observationExit())
)
```

## Exposure cohort: RZV vaccination

This cohort captures any RZV dose. It is used by both arms: the `initiateWithin`
strategy will look for events in this cohort that fall within the grace period,
and the `deferBeyond` strategy will look for events that fall after it.

```{r exposure-cohort}
rzvCohort <- cohort(
  entry = entry(
    drugExposure(rzv, firstOccurrence()),
    observationWindow = continuousObservation(priorDays = 0L)
  ),
  exit = exit(endStrategy = fixedExit(index = "startDate", offsetDays = 0L))
)
```

## Outcome cohort: incident herpes zoster

We restrict to first-ever herpes zoster diagnoses, excluding patients with any
prior herpes zoster to ensure incident cases only.

```{r outcome-cohort}
herpesZosterCohort <- cohort(
  entry = entry(
    conditionOccurrence(herpesZoster, firstOccurrence()),
    observationWindow = continuousObservation(priorDays = 0L)
  ),
  attrition = attrition(
    "No prior herpes zoster" = withAll(
      exactly(0, conditionOccurrence(herpesZoster),
              duringInterval(eventStarts(-Inf, -1L)))
    )
  ),
  exit = exit(endStrategy = fixedExit(index = "startDate", offsetDays = 0L))
)
```

## Assembling the cohort set

`makeCohortSet()` assigns sequential cohort definition IDs and returns a
data frame compatible with `CohortGenerator`.

```{r cohort-set}
# Cohort IDs: 1 = JAK new users, 2 = RZV, 3 = herpes zoster
# makeCohortSet() derives cohort names from the R variable names
allCohorts <- makeCohortSet(jakNewUsers, rzvCohort, herpesZosterCohort)
```

For a real study, include 20–50 negative control outcome cohorts alongside
the primary outcome cohort to support empirical calibration. These can be
pulled from the OHDSI `PhenotypeLibrary`:

```{r negative-controls, eval=FALSE}
library(PhenotypeLibrary)

# Example: fetch a set of negative control outcomes known to be unaffected
# by JAK inhibitor use
negativeControlIds <- c(372924L, 73560L, 201606L)  # illustrative IDs only
ncCohorts <- getPlCohortDefinitionSet(negativeControlIds)

allCohorts <- dplyr::bind_rows(allCohorts, ncCohorts)
```

---

# Generating cohorts

With cohort definitions in hand, we use `CohortGenerator` to create the
cohort tables and instantiate all cohorts on the CDM.

```{r generate}
cohortTableNames <- CohortGenerator::getCohortTableNames(cohortTable)

CohortGenerator::createCohortTables(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTableNames     = cohortTableNames
)

CohortGenerator::generateCohortSet(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cdmDatabaseSchema    = cdmDatabaseSchema,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTableNames     = cohortTableNames,
  cohortDefinitionSet  = allCohorts
)
```

Check cohort counts before proceeding. Very low counts in either the index
or outcome cohort are an early warning that concept sets may need refinement.

```{r counts}
CohortGenerator::getCohortCounts(
  connectionDetails    = connectionDetails,
  cohortDatabaseSchema = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  cohortTable          = cohortTableNames$cohortTable
)
```

---

# Defining the CCW analysis

Every analytical choice is captured in a hierarchy of settings objects that
can be validated, serialized to JSON, and reproduced across sites.

## Treatment strategy arms

`createArmDefinition()` specifies the protocol each clone is assigned to follow.

```{r arms}
# RZV concept IDs to exclude from IPCW covariates so the vaccine does not
# predict its own censoring
rzvConceptIds <- c(1160056L, 1160057L)

armVaccinate <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "rzv_within_90",
  strategyType = "initiateWithin",
  gracePeriod  = 90L,
  label        = "RZV within 90 days of JAK inhibitor start"
)

armDeferred <- createArmDefinition(
  armId        = "no_rzv_within_90",
  strategyType = "deferBeyond",
  gracePeriod  = 90L,
  label        = "No RZV within 90 days"
)
```

## Data extraction

```{r db-args}
dbArgs <- createGetDbCloneCensorWeightDataArgs(
  washoutPeriod     = 365L,
  covariateSettings = FeatureExtraction::createDefaultCovariateSettings(
    excludedCovariateConceptIds = rzvConceptIds,
    addDescendantsToExclude     = TRUE
  )
)
```

## Study population

```{r pop-args}
studyPopArgs <- createCreateStudyPopulationArgs(
  removeSubjectsWithPriorOutcome = TRUE,
  priorOutcomeLookback           = 365L,
  minDaysAtRisk                  = 1L,
  riskWindowEnd                  = 730L,
  endAnchor                      = "cohort start"
)
```

## Cloning and censoring

```{r clone-args}
cloneArgs <- createCreateClonesAndCensorArgs(
  arms           = list(armVaccinate, armDeferred),
  intervalLength = 30L
)
```

## IPCW weights

```{r weight-args}
weightArgs <- createCreateCensoringWeightsArgs(
  trim      = c(0.01, 0.99),
  maxWeight = 10
)
```

## Outcome model

```{r model-args}
modelArgs <- createFitOutcomeModelArgs(
  modelType         = "cox",
  varianceEstimator = "robust"
)
```

## Full analysis specification

```{r analysis}
analysis <- createCcwAnalysis(
  analysisId                     = "main_90day",
  description                    = "Primary: RZV within 90 days vs. deferred",
  getDbCloneCensorWeightDataArgs = dbArgs,
  createStudyPopulationArgs      = studyPopArgs,
  createClonesAndCensorArgs      = cloneArgs,
  createCensoringWeightsArgs     = weightArgs,
  fitOutcomeModelArgs            = modelArgs
)
```

## Target–arm–outcome linkage

`createTargetComparatorOutcome()` links cohort IDs to the analysis. The
`indexCohortId` is the JAK inhibitor new-user cohort. Both arms use the same
`targetCohortId` and `comparatorCohortId` (the RZV cohort) — the arm
strategy determines how each clone interprets initiation events from that
cohort.

```{r tao}
tao <- createTargetComparatorOutcome(
  indexCohortId               = 1L,   # JAK inhibitor new users
  targetCohortId           = 2L,   # RZV (treatment arm)
  comparatorCohortId          = 2L,   # RZV (comparator arm, deferBeyond)
  outcomeIds                  = c(3L, negativeControlIds),
  excludedCovariateConceptIds = rzvConceptIds
)
```

## Top-level specification

```{r specs}
specs <- createCcwAnalysesSpecifications(
  ccwAnalysisList      = list(analysis),
  targetArmOutcomeList = list(tao)
)
```

---

# Running the analysis

`runCcwAnalyses()` iterates over every target–arm–outcome × analysis
combination, runs the full CCW pipeline, and writes results to CSV files in
`outputFolder`. If the run is interrupted, re-running the same call will skip
any combinations already written.

```{r run}
outputFolder <- "jak_rzv_results"

runCcwAnalyses(
  connectionDetails       = connectionDetails,
  cdmDatabaseSchema       = cdmDatabaseSchema,
  targetDatabaseSchema    = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  targetTable             = cohortTableNames$cohortTable,
  outcomeDatabaseSchema   = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  outcomeTable            = cohortTableNames$cohortTable,
  exposureDatabaseSchema  = cohortDatabaseSchema,
  exposureTable           = cohortTableNames$cohortTable,
  ccwAnalysesSpecifications = specs,
  outputFolder            = outputFolder,
  databaseId              = "synpuf",
  negativeControlOutcomeIds = negativeControlIds
)
```

---

# Diagnostics

## Attrition

```{r attrition}
ccwData <- loadCloneCensorWeightData(file.path(outputFolder, "ccwData_main_90day_t1"))
getAttritionTable(ccwData)
```

## Covariate balance

IPCW should reduce covariate imbalance between the arms. The Love plot
displays standardized mean differences (SMD) for all baseline covariates
before and after weighting. Well-balanced covariates have |SMD| < 0.1.

```{r balance, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
results <- importFromCsv(outputFolder)
smd     <- results$ccw_standardized_difference

smd_before <- smd[smd$weighted == 0, ]
smd_after  <- smd[smd$weighted == 1, ]

plotLovePlot(smd_before, smd_after)
```

## Kaplan–Meier curves

```{r km, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
plotKaplanMeier(results$ccw_kaplan_meier)
```

## Minimum detectable relative risk

```{r mdrr}
plotMdrr(results$ccw_power_mdrr)
```

---

# Empirical calibration

When negative control outcomes are supplied via `negativeControlOutcomeIds`,
`runCcwAnalyses()` automatically fits a systematic error model and returns
calibrated p-values and confidence intervals alongside the uncalibrated
estimates. To inspect the calibration:

```{r calibration, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
plotCalibration(
  logRr   = log(results$ccw_outcome_model$estimate),
  seLogRr = (log(results$ccw_outcome_model$upper_95) -
             log(results$ccw_outcome_model$lower_95)) / (2 * qnorm(0.975)),
  trueLogRr = 0  # negative controls have true HR = 1
)
```

---

# Results

```{r results}
om <- results$ccw_outcome_model
om[om$analysis_id == "main_90day_t1_o3",
   c("analysis_id", "model_type", "estimate", "lower_95", "upper_95",
     "p_value", "calibrated_p_value")]
```

---

# Saving and sharing the specification

The full analysis specification can be serialized to JSON for sharing across
sites or checking into version control.

```{r save}
analysisFile <- "jak_rzv_analysis_list.json"
taoFile      <- "jak_rzv_tao_list.json"

saveCcwAnalysisList(list(analysis), analysisFile)
saveTargetComparatorOutcomeList(list(tao), taoFile)
```

To reconstruct the specification in a new session:

```{r load}
reloadedAnalyses <- loadCcwAnalysisList(analysisFile)
reloadedTao      <- loadTargetComparatorOutcomeList(taoFile)
```
